# Public API and entry points {#sec-entry-points}

The library exposes four functions. Three small adapters wrap them for the places
where QViz runs. This page lists both, with their signatures and the reason each
adapter exists.

## The public API {.unnumbered}

`source/backend/__init__.py` is the only import that code outside the library
needs.

```python
from backend import compile, export, load_circuit, sample
```

| Function | Module | Takes | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `load_circuit(text)` | `importer` | OpenQASM 2 or 3 text | a `QuantumCircuit` |
| `compile(backend, qc, *, entangler, strategy, shots, allow_paid, allow_remote)` | `compiler` | a backend object and a circuit | the dictionary of the JSON contract |
| `export(data)` | `exporter` | that dictionary | JSON text |
| `sample(data, step, shots)` | `sampler` | the dictionary and a step | a `dict` of bit strings and counts |

`__version__` is also exported. Each function is documented on the page of its
module.

Two points are worth knowing before the adapters.

- `compile` receives `backend` as an argument. It never imports or creates one,
  because Qollab injects the object as a global of `main.py`.
- `import backend` is never written in `main.py`. It would replace the injected
  variable. The form `from backend import compile` is safe.

## `qollab_api.py` {#sec-qollab-api .unnumbered}

`qollab_api.py` holds the functions that both `main.py` and the pages of the
viewer call. It exists so that the logic lives in one place. Its functions take
and return plain values and **JSON text**, never dictionaries.

| Function | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `CIRCUITS` | The example circuits by name: `bell`, `bell_distant`, `ghz3`, `ghz16`, `layered16`. |
| `build_circuit(name)` | Builds one of them; an unknown name raises `QVizError`. |
| `parse_entangler(value)` | Turns `"auto"`, `"ms"` or `"zz"` into `None`, `"ms"` or `"zz"`. Any other text is an error, never a silent default. |
| `circuits()` | The selector entries as JSON: `[{"file": …, "label": …}]`. |
| `run(backend, circuit, shots, entangler)` | Compiles an example and returns the JSON text. |
| `run_qasm(backend, qasm, shots, entangler)` | Compiles an OpenQASM text, locally (`allow_remote=False`), and returns the JSON text. |
| `sample_step(visualization, step, shots)` | Measures a step of a JSON text and returns `[[bitstring, count], …]` as JSON. |

The reply of `sample_step` is a list of pairs and not an object. A JavaScript
object reorders integer-like keys (`"10"` before `"11"`), which would lose the
order from the most frequent outcome down.

## `main.py` {.unnumbered}

`main.py` is the entry point when the project is uploaded to Qollab as a Python
project.

```python
def main(circuit: str = "bell", shots: int = 1024, entangler: str = "auto", step: int = 0) -> None:
    ...
```

Because the parameters have strict annotations, Qollab draws a form for them in
the QPU dialog. The function compiles an example circuit, prints the backend, the
size, the time and the JSON (only its size if there are more than 30 steps), then
measures one step and prints the most frequent outcomes. It is the only place in
the project, apart from the scripts, that calls `print`.

The signature is on one line because Qollab requires it. For that reason,
`.flake8` ignores `E501` for this file only.

## `resources/scripts/server.py` {.unnumbered}

`make server` starts this file. It serves the repository like
`python -m http.server`, and adds two routes that call the same functions as
Qollab, on the built-in simulator.

| Route | Body | Query | Reply |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/compile` | OpenQASM text | `shots`, `entangler` | the JSON of the visualization |
| `POST /api/sample` | the JSON of a visualization | `step`, `shots` | the list of pairs of `sample_step` |
| `OPTIONS /api/compile`, `OPTIONS /api/sample` | none | none | `204` with `Allow: POST, OPTIONS` |

A circuit that cannot be compiled answers `400` with `{"error": "…"}`, and an
unexpected failure answers `500` with the same shape. A negative or non-numeric
`Content-Length` answers `400`, and a body over the limit answers `413`. The server
listens on `127.0.0.1` only, sends `Cache-Control: no-store`, and redirects `/` to
`/source/frontend/index.html`.

It is a development tool. Qollab never runs it.

## The other tools {.unnumbered}

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `resources/scripts/package_qollab.py` | Builds `qollab/`, the JS project uploaded to Qollab. See [The viewer on Qollab](../frontend/qollab.qmd). |
| `resources/scripts/generate_outputs.py` | Writes the JSON of the example circuits to `out/`, with `out/manifest.json`. |
| `resources/scripts/demo_<module>.py` | A readable demonstration of one stage. See [Demos](../development/demos.qmd). |
| `resources/scripts/_common.py` | The helpers that the demos share. |

## Choosing the right entry point {.unnumbered}

| If the goal is to… | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Compile a circuit from Python code | `compile` and `export` from `backend` |
| Read a `.qasm` file | `load_circuit`, then `compile` |
| Measure a step of a JSON already produced | `sample` |
| Check a backend on Qollab and read the JSON | the Python project (`main.py`) |
| Show the viewer to someone | the JS project (`make qollab`), or `make server` locally |
